findings.message: "leaves meaningful room to grow" is a passive-softening phrase that implies a low baseline without stating it neutrally. Rewrite as a direct observation: e.g. "structured data depth and discovery readiness require further development before citation-ready status is achievable."
findings.context: "machines can discover and parse dotfusion.com pages with high pipeline reliability, though structured data depth and discovery readiness leave meaningful room to grow before citation-ready status is within reach."

findings.message: "Color" is an American spelling. The report uses British/neutral English throughout ("analysing", "optimisation", "recognised"). Replace with "colour" or, preferably, rephrase to avoid the word altogether in a neutral-register report.
findings.context: Inline CSS preview in the Inline Code Duplicates table: `:root{--toastify-color-light: #fff;--toastify-color-dark: #1` — note this is inside a code-literal cell, so it may be exempt as a quoted artefact. However, the word also appears in narrative prose in Appendix C: "no image in the audited set carries both native `loading="lazy"` and a JavaScript lazyload placeholder" — verify whether any free-standing narrative instance of "color" exists outside code literals before actioning.

findings.message: "Catalogue Visibility improvements and metadata tuning that compound over time" is pure domain framing. There is no data anchor — no score, header name, URL, selector, or count — in this Next Steps bullet. The phrase could appear unchanged in any web audit report for any site. Replace with a reference to specific findings already named in the report (e.g. "address the Open Graph gap flagged at 0% cross-page consistency and the Service provider property missing on 5 pages").
findings.context: Next Steps › Recommended Actions: "Review Priority 2-3 findings: Catalogue Visibility improvements and metadata tuning that compound over time"

findings.message: "Consider optional enhancements: optional patterns that give a early-mover opportunity in AI search" names only a domain (AI search) with no mechanism, selector, artefact, or score. There is no data anchor anywhere in this bullet. The Optional Enhancements section above does contain specific items (sameAs, potentialAction, Content-Signal directives), but this Next Steps bullet does not reference any of them by name. Replace with a pointer to those named enhancements.
findings.context: Next Steps › Recommended Actions: "Consider optional enhancements: optional patterns that give a early-mover opportunity in AI search"

findings.message: "a strong foundations to build on" contains a grammatical error that reads as a generation artefact (singular/plural mismatch: "a strong foundations"). This should read "strong foundations to build on". While not a hyperbole category issue per se, it signals unreviewed AI output; flag under exaggeration as a copy-quality indicator consistent with LLM-rewriter output.
findings.context: What's Working Well: "Across the audited set, dotfusion.com demonstrates a strong foundations to build on, with SEO scoring at 86/100..."

findings.message: "warrants attention" applied to a score band is mild failure-framing. The score is stated numerically (49/100) which is neutral, but adding "a band that warrants attention" editorialises beyond the data. Remove the evaluative gloss and let the score speak; or use neutral opportunity framing: "the 49/100 band has the most headroom for improvement."
findings.context: Priority 4 Finding: "We score Semantic Structure at 49/100, a band that warrants attention."
